doc.title: Tom Scott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]

chapter: Mulligan, Brookmeyer and early studio career
title: Soloing with the North Texas lab band at Montreux 1970 and sitting in with Gerry Mulligan
summary: Bob Thiele arranged for Scott to solo with the North Texas State Lab Band at Montreux, where he sat in with idol Mulligan.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Were there some aha moments, we might call them epiphanies now, but you mentioned something, we spoke briefly on the phone and you talked about a circumstance with Gerry Mulligan and Bob Brookmeyer.
Can you revisit that for me, because I found it really interesting.

Absolutely. Well see I had met, well let me back up a little bit — I did two albums for Bob Thiele, Impulse Records, actually Oliver Nelson, God bless him, he provided the opportunity for Bob Thiele, the founder or at least — yeah I think he was the founder of Impulse Records, which of course was the label for all of John Coltrane’s work until he passed, you know Eric Dolphy, Oliver Nelson, Charlie Mingus, just like a whole — the jazz cream of the crop, right? So this was such a privilege to be on this label. And Bob called me and said, listen, I’ve arranged for you to solo with the [extraneous buzz] — bye — arranged for me to solo on — or maybe I should go in another room. Anyway no, arranged for me to solo with the North Texas State Lab Band under the direction of a guy named Leon Breeden, who was a great guy. You may remember that name. He was fabulous. I loved him. So I flew a plane to Montreux, Switzerland where they were part of the Montreux Jazz Festival in 1970, and I played with the lab band. Gerry Mulligan
was there and I swear this is like, in fact I’ve got the picture here somewhere, oh yeah it’s up there — if you could see that, it’s a little hard to see let me see if I could —
Yeah if you moved your screen a bit.

Yeah that’s me there and that’s Gerry Mulligan. He invited me to sit in with him at Montreux. And I was just like oh my God, because he had been an idol of mine for — my first saxophone was the baritone sax.
